questions.question: What is ethnography, and how can it help us learn about hunter-gatherers of long ago?
questions.expected_answer: Ethnography is the study of a living group of people by spending a long time with them, learning their language and recording their way of life. It helps because some ways of life change slowly, so watching people who hunt and gather today can explain objects and rock paintings from long ago, such as the stone with a hole used to weigh down a digging stick.

questions.question: Describe three things researchers learnt from San communities in the Kalahari.
questions.expected_answer: They lived in small groups of related families and moved with the seasons; women gathered much of the food while men hunted with small bows and poisoned arrows; meat was shared so everyone got some; and healers danced into a trance at healing dances while women clapped and sang.

questions.question: Give two reasons why we must be careful when using ethnography to understand the past.
questions.expected_answer: People today are not exactly like people long ago, because the San of the Kalahari had traded with herders and farmers and their land had been affected by governments and farms. Different San groups lived in different ways, and the researcher's own ideas could affect what they wrote.
